newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian panel to discuss allowing derivatives - paper.
newsitem.headline: Indian panel to discuss allowing derivatives - paper.

text.p: A committee set up by the Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI) to weigh the pros and cons of introducing derivatives trading in India was to meet on Thursday, the Economic Times said.
The newspaper said on Thursday that the main issues on the agenda would be whether or not mutual funds should be permitted to trade derivatives and if current law allowed them to do so.
India does not allow futures and options trading but SEBI, the stock market regulator, intends to start after examining the issues.

The newspaper said the committee was also expected to discuss whether a new exchange needed to be set up for derivatives trading or if current stock exchanges were sufficient, and what what qualifications would be required of brokers wanting to trade derivatives.
The panel was also considering the possibility of a centralised clearing house for derivatives trading, it said.
SEBI expects the committee to submit a report within three months, but that may not be possible, the newspaper said.

India's National Stock Exchange submitted a proposal to SEBI last year in hopes of introducing futures and options by December, but SEBI decided it wanted to study the pros and cons of introducing derivatives first, it said.
